tests.reason: Unique production focus-lifetime regression: a child cleanup must not orphan the still-visible shell target, and stopped holds must not revive a previous target.

sixBar.independentContract: The visible/focused chat must remain the target for keyboard and right-rail actions for the lifetime of the shell's published view, even when the child chat view performs a cleanup/remount. Historical regression commit 02ad58e19b73feb6313be6f94295fcc4ef281054 records StrictMode cleanup leaving the Device panel at 'Open an agent chat' beside an open chat and disabling chat shortcuts. Devices phase-1 design §§10.1–10.2 independently requires the Device panel/follow target to be the visible chat.
sixBar.realRegressionDetection: Calling releaseActiveChatTab('a') while the shell still holds visible chat 'a' must leave activeChatTab() as 'a'; losing the restoring subscription fails that literal assertion. After moving to 'b', old-view release cannot steal the new target. Stopping holds and publishing no chat must yield null; a leaked old hold instead restores an old id and fails the final assertion.
sixBar.independentOracle: The expected ids 'a', 'b' and null are literal user/shell choices and the lifetime contract, not values obtained from holdActiveChatTab internals, listener counts, production constants or a mock implementing the focus policy.
sixBar.stableSeam: The production-used holdActiveChatTab/releaseActiveChatTab lifecycle and public activeChatTab value. MainView's effect owns the hold; AgentChatView cleanup releases; composer/banner keyboard handlers, right-rail chat-target and Devices use-follow-agent consume the published focus.
sixBar.refactorResistance: Observes active session identity after lifecycle actions and returned unsubscribe, with no source grep, effect inventory, listener implementation, markup/layout, private callback shape or exact copy requirement. A different internal focus registry preserving the same lifecycle behavior continues to pass.
sixBar.uniqueProtection: This is the only test invoking holdActiveChatTab (repository-wide test search). Existing set/release/active-tab derivation cases do not hold a shell claim across child cleanup; Devices follow tests supply visibility and do not exercise restoration after release. The latter transition and hold teardown therefore have no stronger remaining owner. The non-owner release step also verifies the handover within that held lifecycle rather than adding a separate repeated scenario.

contractSources: packages/ui/src/components/main/MainView.tsx effect ownership and packages/ui/src/components/agent-chat/AgentChatView.tsx cleanup (current call-site evidence)
tests.performanceImpact: One synchronous registry lifecycle sequence; no browser, server, filesystem, network, polling or elapsed-time wait. No timing improvement claimed.
